findings.text: A single decision routine determines the migration source for one balancing pass. It refreshes domain wide summaries, applies ordered exemption and forcing checks driven by group categories idleness and capacity, then asks for an imbalance amount. When no busy peer exists or an exemption applies it reports no source and clears the amount, otherwise it returns the busiest peer when the amount is positive.

Group category is chosen by strict precedence. Saturation outranks cache locality need, which outranks externally flagged skew, which outranks asymmetric packing need, which outranks SMT spreading need, which outranks misfit load presence, which outranks lack of headroom, with spare as the default. Only the first satisfied condition determines the result.
If the local category is ordered as busier than the busiest peer category the pass stops without movement, independent of load values. This ordering check precedes average based fairness logic.

When the local group shows saturation, movement requires local average below peer average and below domain average derived from total load over total capacity scaled to the capacity unit. A further tolerance suppresses movement when peer average does not exceed local average by the configured imbalance percentage.

When the busiest child prefers sibling placement and the local group has spare, a sibling imbalance greater than one forces movement, as does a cache locality need in the busiest group. The sibling measure is zero unless the caller is idle and the busiest group has runnable tasks, equal core counts yield a saturated difference of runnable counts, unequal counts yield a core normalized and rounded value, and an empty local group with multiple remote runnable tasks is promoted to a minimum that forces action.

For a non saturated busiest group a non idle caller never pulls, letting an idle peer act instead. Movement is also suppressed when the idle CPU counts differ by at most one on multi CPU groups, and when the busiest hierarchical runnable count equals one indicating no waiting task.

A cache sharing mismatch between local and busiest groups can force movement when the busiest group needs SMT spreading, allowing a non sharing CPU to pull from a sharing CPU. Separately a remote sharing group with more than one hierarchical runnable task is flagged for SMT spreading only on idle passes, and null group handles never report a mismatch.

Domain summary initialization leaves local statistics untouched for later full assignment, clears total load and capacity and peer handles, and presets the busiest comparison baseline to spare with the largest possible idle CPU count so that later selection starts from the least busy assumption.

Domain aggregation walks every group once, marks the group containing the destination CPU as local, refreshes local capacity on non newly idle passes or when the refresh deadline has elapsed, accumulates total load capacity and utilization, retains the best non local candidate as busiest, derives sibling preference from the busiest flags, classifies NUMA groups for fallback queue handling, and at the root level publishes overload and overutilization indicators while non root levels only publish overutilization when present.

Group aggregation zeroes its output then scans only CPUs common to the group span and the allowed set, summing load utilization runnable and hierarchical counts plus total runnable, counting idle CPUs via a zero runnable plus idle check, deferring overload publication to root domain scans with more than one runnable, and computing average load solely for saturated groups as load scaled to capacity unit over capacity.

Misfit load is recorded only for non local groups. Under asymmetric capacity it tracks the largest misfit load among member queues when the destination capacity clearly exceeds the group maximum, and always marks root overload when any misfit exists. Without asymmetric capacity it applies only on idle passes for queues holding a single runnable task on reduced capacity, tracking the largest observed load.

Capacity refresh schedules the next update by converting the domain interval to timer units and clamping it within a lower bound of one and a global maximum. Leaf domains delegate to per CPU scaling, non leaf NUMA domains sum per CPU capacities with minima and maxima over the span, and non leaf non NUMA domains sum child group cached values.

Per CPU capacity starts from actual capacity minus real time and deadline usage and interrupt usage, never drops below one, is published to the run queue record, and updates the local group cached capacity triple with identical values. One build scales interrupt usage proportionally while the alternate build ignores interrupt pressure.

CPU utilization starts from the fair queue average, optionally adds or removes a migrating task contribution depending on direction relative to the examined CPU, optionally raises the result to the runnable average when boosting, optionally raises it to an estimated value that simulates enqueue or dequeue of the task, and finally caps the result to architectural capacity. Overutilization means the fair utilization does not fit within the allowed maximum clamp.

When energy aware scheduling is disabled the domain is always considered overutilized for balancing decisions, per CPU overutilization is always false, and attempts to publish the domain overutilization flag are ignored without tracing. When enabled the flag is read and written with single copy accessors and publication emits a trace event.

Cache aware group statistics are recorded only when cache tracking is enabled, the pass is not newly idle, and the current domain parent matches the last level cache domain of the destination. The first CPU of the group span locates the shared cache record, and utilization and capacity are published there only on change using single copy accessors.

The domain summary observed in these fragments carries handles for busiest and local groups, total load and capacity accumulators, a domain average, a sibling preference flag, plus embedded local and busiest group summaries. The balancing environment carries destination CPU and queue, domain handle, allowed CPU set, idleness state, imbalance result, fallback queue type, and a destination core idle flag.

The group summary observed here carries load utilization and runnable sums, hierarchical and total runnable counts, idle CPU count, weight and capacity, average load, category, overload and overutilization flags, misfit load, packing and spreading and locality flags, plus NUMA runnable counts and cache destination counts under respective options.

Capacity dominance requires roughly a five percent margin expressed by factors 1024 versus 1078. Averages scale load by the fixed capacity unit. Imbalance tolerance uses percent base one hundred. Initialization uses the largest unsigned values for idle count and capacity minima. Refresh intervals clamp to at least one tick up to a global maximum.

Overlapping NUMA groups violate the domain average assumption and can misdirect the saturated fairness check. Zero scaled capacity must be raised to one to avoid division hazards in average computation. Estimated utilization has a small race between migration dequeue and wakeup path selection that can double count or miss a task contribution. Capacity and utilization observations rely on potentially stale cached and lock free reads.

Group capacity refresh, interrupt capacity scaling in both build variants, and fair utilization query are globally visible for use outside this file, while the remaining helpers in these fragments are file local or header inline.

These fragments take no explicit locks. Shared scalar and pointer observations use single copy accessors and RCU dereference, including overutilization flags, asymmetric preference, cache hierarchy handles, and utilization averages, implying callers provide any required RCU read protection and exclusion for mutable run queue and group state.

Asymmetric packing is considered only for non local groups on idle passes with hierarchical runnable tasks, is rejected for sharing groups unless exactly one member is busy, and otherwise defers to a domain level asymmetric preference comparison for the destination CPU.

Saturation requires more runnable tasks than weight plus either utilization or runnable pressure exceeding capacity after applying the imbalance percentage, and under energy awareness additionally requires at least one overutilized CPU. Headroom exists when runnable tasks are fewer than weight or when capacity comfortably covers utilization despite runnable pressure.
Reduced capacity handling applies only to queues with exactly one hierarchical runnable task and then defers to a CPU capacity check against the domain.
Group span access converts the internal group mask storage to a CPU mask handle for iteration and membership tests.
Saturated subtraction reduces the pointed value by the smaller of its current content and the subtrahend, never wrapping below zero, and evaluates its arguments through local temporaries.
